| Case | Pattern | What the engine was | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Radico Khaitan (2016→2026) | Mix shift + deleveraging in an out-of-favour company | Earnings ~7.5x × P/E ~5x (approx.) | Twin engine; thesis ≠ timing (8 dead years first) |
| NVIDIA (2016→2026) | Hidden fast segment inside a cyclical company | Mostly earnings after 2023 | Earnings alone can carry a multibagger; expect 50%+ drawdowns |
| Eicher / Royal Enfield | New-CEO product reset of a stagnant brand | Fastest Wealth Creator 2009–14 ([MOSL](https://www.motilaloswal.com/content/dam/mofsl-website-adobe/investor-relations/wealth-creation/wc19.pdf)); ~86x from 2005 ([PrimeInvestor](https://primeinvestor.in/?p=56537)) | Read management change plus channel evidence |
| Defence PSUs (2020–24) | Policy shift (indigenisation) | Rally "largely driven by valuation rerating rather than faster growth" ([Business Standard 2023](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/rally-in-listed-defence-stocks-yet-to-be-backed-by-earnings-growth-123071300913_1.html)); HAL 28x forward vs 14x 5-yr avg in 2025 ([Business Today](https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/mazagon-dock-hal-bdl-bel-share-price-targets-for-9-defence-stocks-ahead-of-q4-results-471974-2025-04-15)) | Multiple-led moves need earnings to catch up |
| Deepak Nitrite (2020–21) | Import-substitution capex + China+1 | +135% in 6 months to Mar 2021 ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/deepak-nitrite-analysts-see-further-upside-despite-135-rally-in-6-months-121030500331_1.html)); FY26 profit down ([Upstox](https://upstox.com/stocks/deepak-nitrite-ltd-share-price/INE288B01029)) | A correct thesis meets cyclical spread compression; the exit matters |
| Suzlon (2008) | Green-energy policy tailwind | **−99.6%**, from ₹430.92 (2008) to ₹1.51 (2020) ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/suzlon-energy-shares-down-96-in-5-years-this-stock-rebounded-42x-heres-why-456906-2024-12-11)) | Same story as the winners, killed by leverage |
| Amazon (1999–2009) | Platform compounder | −94%, then 10 years to regain the 1999 high ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2016/06/26/amazon-stocks-history-the-importance-of-patience.aspx)) | Survivorship: most dot-com names never came back |

body:
This is a sector-level view; I did not deep-dive individual companies.
- **Oil marketing companies (HPCL / BPCL / IOC):** crude is priced in USD while retail pricing is administered, so they absorb the currency hit.
- **Airlines (InterGlobe / SpiceJet):** both fuel and lease rentals are in USD. A weaker rupee together with high crude hits them twice.
- **Paints and crude-derivative users (Asian Paints, Berger, Indigo Paints, Kansai):** raw materials such as TiO2 and monomers are imported or priced in USD, and competition limits price increases.
- **Edible-oil importers (AWL Agri):** palm and soy oil are imported, and margins are thin.
- **Consumer electronics and durables assemblers with weak pass-through:** imported components and chips. EMS players with contractual pass-through are less affected.
- **Any company with unhedged ECB or USD debt and only rupee revenue.**
- **Partial losers:** low-value bulky exporters (home textiles, shrimp). Freight at 3x and buyer price-downs are taking the rupee gain, as Avanti, Apex, Indo Count and Gokaldas already show.

body:
- **Works and is scriptable now:** the NSE corporate APIs (announcements, shareholding, pledge, SAST, PIT, results, bulk/block) on `www.nseindia.in` with browser headers and no cookie; the BSE API over HTTP/2 with Sec-Fetch headers; transcript PDFs from both exchanges plus `pdftotext`; the screener.in Concalls index (no login needed); ICRA and CRISIL rationales; FADA, NPP, PPAC, SIAM, the Play-store install bucket, and Google Trends RSS.
- **Doesn't work from here:** NSE live quotes; India Ratings (SPA); clean CARE endpoints; Grid-India, e-way bill, IPA ports, JPC, data.gov.in, NPCI and the Trends explore API (most of these look like geo-blocks or IP throttling, so retry from an Indian IP); eaindustry (broken TLS).
- **Method:** the India evidence says concall *tone* is priced but uninformative, so the durable edge is a **multi-year promise-vs-delivery ledger, filing diffs and ownership-change alerts**, plus *targeted*, PIT-safe scuttlebutt on the few flags that matter.

Seed records: `memdb/seeds/2026-11-19_edge_methods.json` (15 records: 5 source, 7 insight, 3 strategy).
title: edge_methods_data_access › Bottom line

body:
- **Sources.** Ten earnings-call transcripts, from Q1 FY25 (call held 2024-08-09) to Q2 FY27 (call held 2026-11-05), were pulled with `tools/nse_fetch.py transcripts UNIPARTS --download` and converted with `pdftotext -layout`. The Q4 FY24 call (2024-05-28) was read for background only.
- **Numbers.** Actual figures come from the screener.in consolidated page (quarterly P&L, annual P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and ratios), plus the CFO's figures in each later call. Ratios were re-derived by hand: FY25 OPM, H1/H2 sums, capex totals, ROCE, aftermarket ₹ from share-of-revenue figures.
- **Extraction.** Each call was condensed into speaker turns, with management turns kept in full and analyst questions shortened. Every forward-looking statement that had a metric or a direction was logged, by hand, against the schema in `edge_methods_data_access.md` §2.
- **Scoring.** Status is one of: delivered (+1), partly (+0.5), missed (−1), moved-goalpost (−1.5), silently-dropped (−1.5) or pending. The weight of each promise is specificity score (1–3) × materiality (1–3) × 0.5^(quarters elapsed / 8).

`person:group-emami` · flag: **mixed** · confidence: verified · tickers: EMAMILTD, EMAMIPAP, EMAMIREAL

Flag: MIXED. Kolkata group whose cash-rich FMCG company Emami Ltd (Navratna, Boroplus, Zandu) has been the collateral behind diversification into cement, power, paper, real estate, edible oils and hospitals. Pledge cycle: promoter pledges on Emami Ltd shares rose through 2016-2018; in Feb-2019 the Agarwal and Goenka families sold ~10% of Emami for ~Rs 1,600 cr explicitly to pare debt of other group companies (Emami Cement, Emami Power) and release pledges; Emami Cement was later sold to Nuvoco (2020, ~Rs 5,500 cr) to deleverage the group. Pledges have not gone away: an aggregator shows ~16% of promoter holdings pledged in 2026, and a BSE disclosure records a fresh pledge of ~2.16 cr shares (~4.95% of equity) by promoter entity Diwakar Finvest on 9-Jan-2026 (verify lender on SAST). At the listed-company level Emami has paid steady dividends and run buybacks (2022, 2023) and no regulator findings of diversion were found. Emami Realty (listed) is loss-making and leveraged. Investor read: Emami Ltd's own operations and minority treatment are acceptable; the risk channel is promoter-level borrowing against Emami shares to fund unlisted/other ventures -- a repeating pattern (2018-19, again 2026). Track pledge % quarterly.

- **red flags:** recurring promoter pledges for group ventures; 2019 stake sale to repay group debt
- **good conduct:** buybacks, dividends; deleveraging via Emami Cement sale
